facts_of_case: The husband and wife were married in 1976. The husband filed a petition for nullity due to the wife's impotency and refusal to consummate the marriage. A medical report revealed the wife had a second-degree prolapse of the uterus, indicating non-virginity. The husband suspected the wife was concealing facts and that the marriage was brought about by fraud and misrepresentation.

legal_principles.principle: A petition need not mention every detail of the facts
legal_principles.held: Having asserted non-consummation of the marriage, it was not necessary to mention in the petition each and every approach the petitioner made to the respondent and which was repulsed.

legal_principles.principle: Evidence need not be stated in the petition or notice
legal_principles.held: It was sufficient to say generally that from the very first night till the relevant date, there was no consummation of marriage.

keywords: Latin maxim: Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea
use_for_drafting: drafting petition for nullity of marriage
advising client on grounds for divorce
